title: Pad thai
intro: Rice noodles stir-fried with prawns, tamarind and peanuts: sour, sweet and salty at once.

steps.t: Soak the noodles in warm (not boiling) water for 25 minutes, until pliable but still firm. Drain.
steps.label: Soak

steps.t: Meanwhile stir the tamarind, fish sauce and sugar until dissolved. Cube the tofu, chop the garlic and shallot.
Cut the spring onions into 4 cm lengths and roughly chop the peanuts.
Heat 2 tbsp oil in the wok over high heat. Brown the tofu, then the garlic and shallot, then the prawns until pink.
steps.label: Wok

steps.t: Push everything to one side, add the remaining oil, crack in the eggs and scramble until almost set.
Add the noodles and sauce and toss for 3 minutes, until tender and glossy. Add a splash of water if they stick.
steps.label: Noodles

steps.t: Add the bean sprouts and spring onions and toss for 30 seconds. Serve with peanuts, chilli and lime wedges.

tips.t: Cook at most two portions at a time: too many noodles cool the wok and they turn mushy.
Vegetarian: double the tofu, skip the prawns and use soy sauce for fish sauce (then not gluten-free).

title: Homemade shoyu ramen
intro: Chicken stock boosted with kombu and shiitake, soy tare, a jammy egg and crisp pork belly.

steps.t: Put the stock (store-bought is fine) in a pot with kombu, shiitake, sliced ginger, crushed garlic and onion greens. Simmer 30 min.
steps.label: Broth

steps.t: Meanwhile lower the fridge-cold eggs into boiling water and cook for 6½ minutes.
steps.label: Eggs

steps.t: Chill them in iced water, peel and put them in a bag with 2 tbsp soy sauce, 1 tbsp mirin and 3 tbsp water.
Fry the pork belly in a dry pan for 4 minutes per side, until crisp and cooked through. Salt lightly.
steps.label: Pork

steps.t: Make the tare: mix the remaining soy sauce and mirin with the sesame oil and divide between two warm bowls.
Strain the broth and keep it piping hot. Thinly slice the white of the spring onions.
Boil the noodles in plenty of unsalted water for the time on the pack, usually 2–4 minutes. Drain well.
steps.label: Noodles

steps.t: Pour 400 ml boiling broth into each bowl over the tare and stir. Add the noodles and lift them to untangle.
Top with the pork, halved egg, bamboo shoots, nori and spring onion. Serve at once.

tips.t: The eggs are even better marinated overnight: make them the day before.
A teaspoon of chilli oil (rayu) or white pepper in each bowl adds warmth.
The broth freezes for 3 months: make double and ramen is 10 minutes away.

title: Yakisoba
intro: Noodles fried with pork and cabbage in a tangy sauce: Japanese festival street food.

ing.n: thinly sliced pork shoulder or belly

steps.t: Mix the Worcestershire, oyster sauce, ketchup, soy and sugar. Cut the cabbage into 3 cm pieces, the carrot into sticks, slice the onion.
Rinse the noodles under hot water to loosen them. If using dried ramen, boil them 1 minute less than the pack says.
Heat 1 tbsp oil over high heat and fry the pork, cut into pieces, for 3 minutes until browned and cooked through.
steps.label: Pork

steps.t: Add the onion, carrot and cabbage and stir-fry for 3 minutes, until the cabbage is tender but still crisp.
steps.label: Veg

steps.t: Add the noodles and the remaining oil and toss for 2 minutes, letting a few strands crisp up.
steps.label: Noodles

steps.t: Pour in the sauce, add the bean sprouts and toss for 1 minute, until everything is glossy.
Serve topped with aonori and red pickled ginger.

tips.t: Top it with a fried egg for an even more satisfying plate.
Don't stir constantly: leave the noodles still for a few seconds so they colour.

title: Pho bo (beef pho)
intro: Beef broth spiced with star anise and charred ginger, poured boiling over raw sliced beef.

steps.t: Halve the onion and ginger and char them in a dry pan over high heat until blackened in spots.
steps.label: Char

steps.t: Toast the star anise, cinnamon, cloves and coriander seeds in a dry pot for 2 minutes, until fragrant.
steps.label: Spices

steps.t: Add the stock, water, onion, ginger, fish sauce and sugar and simmer gently for 45 minutes.
steps.label: Broth

steps.t: Meanwhile put the beef in the freezer for 15 minutes, then slice it paper-thin across the grain.
steps.label: Freezer

steps.t: Prepare the noodles as directed on the pack, drain and divide between 4 large bowls.
Strain the broth, bring it back to a rolling boil and taste: adjust with fish sauce or salt.
Lay the raw beef over the noodles and ladle the boiling broth over it: it cooks instantly and turns pink.
Bring the bean sprouts, basil, coriander, lime and chilli to the table so everyone dresses their own bowl.

tips.t: The broth must be truly boiling when you pour it: that's what cooks the beef.
Put hoisin and sriracha on the table for those who want them (hoisin often contains gluten).

title: Dan dan noodles
intro: Sichuan noodles with crispy pork, sesame sauce and tingling chilli oil.

steps.t: Toast the Sichuan pepper in a dry pan for 1 minute, until fragrant, then grind it fine.
In each bowl, mix the sesame paste, 2 tbsp soy, chilli oil, vinegar, sugar, grated garlic and half the pepper.
Heat the oil over high heat and fry the pork, breaking it up, for 5 minutes until browned and crisp, with no pink left.
steps.label: Pork

steps.t: Add the Shaoxing wine, 1 tbsp soy and the ya cai and stir-fry for 1 minute, until dry and crumbly.
Boil the noodles for the time on the pack; add the halved pak choi for the last minute.
steps.label: Noodles

steps.t: Add 3 tbsp of the cooking water to each bowl to loosen the sauce, then drain the noodles and greens into the bowls.
Top with the pork, chopped peanuts, spring onions and the rest of the pepper. Mix well before eating.

tips.t: If you can't find ya cai, use 1 tbsp chopped capers: different, but the same salty kick.
Adjust the tingle with Sichuan pepper: it should make your lips slightly numb.

title: Japchae
intro: Chewy sweet potato noodles with stir-fried vegetables, soy and sesame: Korean party food.

steps.t: Boil the noodles for 6 minutes until clear and chewy. Rinse cold, snip with scissors, toss with 1 tbsp sesame oil and 1 tbsp soy.
steps.label: Noodles

steps.t: Blanch the spinach for 30 seconds, cool, squeeze dry and season with salt and 1 tsp sesame oil.
steps.label: Spinach

steps.t: Mix the remaining soy with the sugar, minced garlic, 1 tbsp sesame oil and pepper. Cut the vegetables into thin strips.
Stir-fry the onion and carrot in a little oil for 3 minutes, then the pepper and shiitake for 3 more, until tender-crisp.
steps.label: Veg

steps.t: Add the noodles and sauce and toss for 2 minutes over medium heat, until the sauce is absorbed.
steps.label: Toss

steps.t: Turn off the heat and fold in the spinach, spring onions, remaining sesame oil and seeds. Serve warm or at room temperature.

tips.t: Stir-fry the vegetables separately so each keeps its colour and crunch.
Classic but not vegan: add 150 g beef strips marinated in the same sauce.
Keeps 2 days in the fridge: reheat in a pan with a splash of water to soften the noodles.

title: Cold sesame noodles
intro: Chilled noodles in a creamy sesame, soy and chilli oil sauce, with crunchy cucumber.

steps.t: Boil the noodles for the time on the pack, until tender but still springy.
steps.label: Noodles

steps.t: Drain and rinse under cold water until cold. Drain well and toss with the sesame oil.
Whisk the sesame paste with the warm water until smooth, then add soy, vinegar, sugar, chilli oil, grated garlic and ginger.
Cut the cucumber into matchsticks and slice the spring onions. Roughly chop the peanuts.
Toss the noodles with the sauce and top with cucumber, spring onions, sesame and peanuts. Serve cold.

tips.t: Add cubed smoked tofu or edamame to make it a full meal.
Keep the sauce and noodles separate in the fridge: they last 2 days; dress just before eating.

title: Zaru soba, cold dipping soba
intro: Cold soba dipped in a dashi and soy sauce: Japan's go-to summer lunch.

steps.t: For the dipping sauce, boil the mirin for 1 minute, then add the soy sauce, sugar and dashi and simmer for 1 minute.
steps.label: Sauce

steps.t: Pour the sauce into a bowl, let it cool a little and refrigerate for 30 minutes: it's served cold.
steps.label: Chill

steps.t: Meanwhile bring a large pot of unsalted water to a boil. Slice the spring onions, cut the nori into thin strips, grate the daikon.
Cook the soba as the pack says, about 4½ minutes, stirring; if it foams up, add a splash of cold water.
steps.label: Soba

steps.t: Drain and rinse under cold running water, rubbing with your hands to remove the starch, then plunge into iced water.
Drain very well and pile onto bamboo mats or plates, with the nori on top.
Serve the sauce in small cups with spring onion, wasabi and daikon on the side: dip one bite of soba at a time.

tips.t: At the end, pour some noodle cooking water into the leftover sauce and drink it: that's sobayu.
With 100% buckwheat soba (juwari) and tamari instead of soy sauce, it's gluten-free.
Leftover sauce keeps 4 days in a sealed jar in the fridge.
